memory_lessons.applicability: Use aggregate factor comparisons to motivate a contrasting unroll factor, but do not infer which input pattern benefits without per-pattern timings.
memory_lessons.claim: The visible valid candidates measured 2.2604 µs with two accumulators, 3.0152 µs with three, and 2.8135 µs with four. These aggregate timings show no monotonic improvement with accumulator count; per-pattern effects and the cause are not established by the visible measurements.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate the eight-accumulator candidate, then compare repeated random and decreasing input timings separately under the frozen protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: A scalar eight-way unroll may expose more independent minimum/index chains than the previously measured two-, three-, and four-accumulator candidates, reducing loop-carried dependence on random and decreasing inputs. The lower measured aggregate time for two accumulators (2.2604 µs) than for three (3.0152 µs) or four (2.8135 µs) shows that more chains are not automatically better; eight also raises initialization, fold, and instruction-pressure costs, so correctness and per-pattern measurements are needed to assess the tradeoff.

retained: Added a fixed eight-way scalar scan with eight independent minimum-value and earliest-index accumulators.
Folded the accumulators using signed minimum-value ordering and lowest-index tie-breaking.
Handled n < 8 with a scalar path and processed any trailing elements scalarly after the fold.
Used no explicit SIMD or parallel workers.
